fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Yearbook Survey
fields.features_subheading: Yearbook survey questions gather the quotes and votes that fill student pages. Emergent builds the survey and its table.
fields.feature_1:
Questions grouped by yearbook page

Name the pages the survey feeds, such as superlatives, senior quotes, and the class page. Emergent drafts a section of questions for each one, and you change any question by prompt.
fields.feature_2:
One answer per student on the roster

Load the class roster, and the survey takes one answer per student ID. Students answer one question per screen on a phone, and any repeat from that ID is left out of the count.
fields.feature_3:
Superlatives counted by category

The app counts nominations in each superlative category as they arrive. A tie stays marked on the editors' view until a runoff settles it, then the winner moves to the page list.
fields.feature_4:
Character limits on quotes and memories

Set a limit on senior quotes and memory answers. A student who types past it sees the count turn red and trims the quote before sending it, rather than after the spread is laid out.
fields.feature_5:
Reminders before the deadline

Students who have not answered get an email reminder before the deadline. The adviser gets a Slack list of who is still missing by homeroom, and finished students hear nothing.
fields.feature_6:
A database and code that stay yours

Each answer is a row in a database you own, tagged with name and homeroom. Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. The free tier covers building and publishing.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Schools Run Yearbook Surveys
fields.tab_content_1:
Two seniors tie on 31 for Best Laugh

Wexley High's yearbook staff asks 286 seniors to nominate a classmate in 12 superlative categories. The app checks each ballot against the senior roster and drops a second ballot from the same student. By the deadline 241 of 286 seniors had voted. Best Laugh ended in a 31 to 31 tie, and the staff sent a runoff ballot.
fields.tab_content_2:
22 quotes still missing 9 days before deadline

Every senior at Corvallen Academy sends a yearbook quote of up to 120 characters, and the adviser approves or returns each quote. With 9 days left before the page deadline, 22 of 148 seniors had sent nothing. The app emailed each of them a reminder with a link back to the quote screen.
fields.tab_content_3:
Seven kids who want to be veterinarians, out of 24

Families of the 24 third graders in a class at Ellery Park Elementary answer a 6-question All About Me survey at home. Each child's answers land in a single row, ready for the class page. When the teacher sorted the dream-job answers, 7 of 24 kids said veterinarian, and the page gained a corner for future vets.
fields.tab_content_4:
The 8th grade's top song takes the trends spread

A 5-question trends poll goes to all 488 students at Tarrant Hill Middle School. The app splits every answer by grade. On the song question, the 8th grade's favorite drew 112 votes, more than any song in the 6th or 7th grade, and the yearbook club built its trends spread around it.

fields.howto_title: How to Write Yearbook Survey Questions
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to write yearbook survey questions that every student can answer before the page deadline, then build the survey with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Start from the pages you need to fill
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Give each open question an example
fields.howto_step_1_des: List the yearbook pages the survey has to feed, such as the senior pages or a trends spread. Write only questions whose answers land on one of those pages. Put the page list in your prompt, and Emergent groups the questions to match.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Import the current roster with each student's name as it should print, plus homeroom or grade. Make the first question a check of the printed name. A misspelled name caught in March is a quick fix; caught on the final proof, it is a late correction.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Choose categories a student would be glad to win. Drop any category that could single out a student for looks, grades, or a rumor, even as a joke. Run the final list past the adviser before the ballot opens to the class.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Under every open question, show a sample answer in the length and tone you want, like a one-line memory from homecoming. Students copy the shape of the example. Editors then get answers that fit the page without rewriting them.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Ask for one thing per question
fields.howto_step_5_des: Ask for one song or one memory, not a list. A prompt like favorite moment this year invites a paragraph, while name one moment from this year in a sentence gets a line the editors can print as written.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Close the survey at least 3 weeks before the pages go to layout. That window leaves room for late answers and a superlative runoff. Send the first reminder a week before the survey closes and a second one 2 days out.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Read every answer before it prints
fields.howto_step_7_des: Read each answer before it goes on a page, looking for inside jokes and hidden meanings in senior quotes. Return a quote with a short note and give the student 2 days to send a new one. Keep a log of what was returned and why.

faq_plan.a: Yearbook survey questions are the prompts a yearbook staff sends to students to gather the words for student pages: superlative nominations, senior quotes, and favorite memories. The answers become the text and vote counts printed beside each photo.

faq_plan.q: How do I create yearbook survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Start with the pages the answers will fill, then write one short question per item on each page. To run it, describe the survey to Emergent's AI survey builder, including the roster and the deadline. Emergent builds the survey and the database behind it.

faq_plan.q: Which superlative categories make good yearbook survey questions?
faq_plan.a: The best categories celebrate something a student chose to do or be: Best Smile, Most School Spirit, Most Likely to Travel, Best Laugh, or Most Likely to Start a Business. Keep the ballot to 12 categories or fewer. Seniors finish it in one sitting, and each category draws enough votes to name a winner.

faq_plan.q: How many yearbook survey questions should one survey include?
faq_plan.a: Keep one survey to 15 questions or fewer, which a student can finish on a phone in about 5 minutes. If the staff needs more, split it into a superlatives ballot in the fall and a senior survey for quotes and memories in the spring. Emergent puts no cap on responses, whether 40 students answer or 600.

faq_plan.q: What yearbook survey questions should seniors answer?
faq_plan.a: Seniors should answer the questions behind their own page: their name as it should print, a senior quote, a favorite memory, plans after graduation, and the superlative ballot. Add one question for a senior wills or advice-to-underclassmen section if the book has one.

faq_plan.q: How do I limit superlative yearbook survey questions to one answer per student?
faq_plan.a: Tie each ballot to the student roster instead of an open link. Each senior signs in with a student ID, and the survey accepts one ballot per ID before the count runs. With a survey built on Emergent, the roster and every ballot sit in a database you own, ready for next year's staff.

faq_plan.q: What yearbook survey questions suit elementary students?
faq_plan.a: Short, concrete questions a parent can read aloud suit young students: favorite food, favorite book, a favorite thing about this year, and what they want to be when they grow up. Keep it near 6 questions, and let families answer at home on a phone.

faq_plan.q: Should yearbook survey questions cap how long a senior quote can be?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Set the cap from the space the layout gives each senior, such as 120 characters. Students then write to fit, and editors print the quote as written instead of trimming it. Memory answers can take their own, longer cap.

faq_plan.q: When should yearbook survey questions go out to students?
faq_plan.a: Send them 6 to 8 weeks before the pages are due, which gives students 3 to 5 weeks to answer before the survey closes. A window that long survives a spring break or a testing week, and the survey still closes 3 weeks before layout.

faq_plan.q: Should answers to yearbook survey questions be anonymous?
faq_plan.a: No, not for anything that prints beside a name: a quote or a superlative nomination must be tied to the student. Make a question anonymous only when its result prints as a total, such as a trends poll. Emergent can build both kinds into one survey from a plain-English prompt.

plan.angle: The top 10 is printable question sheets, Pinterest pins and personality quizzes: lists of prompts with nothing to collect, count or chase the answers. This page shows a yearbook adviser, a senior class, an elementary teacher and a middle school staff running yearbook survey questions as an app: one answer per student checked against the roster, superlative votes tallied per category, quotes held to a length limit, and every answer in a table the editors lay out from.
